result.markdown: --- title: "[concordance_index_ci()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} IPCW concordance index with a confidence interval. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_metrics.py#L2077-L2188){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python concordance_index_ci( surv, risk, *, data=None, cause=None, tau=None, conf_level=0.95, transform="logit" ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Computes the Uno-style IPCW concordance and derives the standard error from the influence function decomposition. The confidence interval is constructed on the logit (default), log, or identity scale and back-transformed. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv | Outcome | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A `Surv` response. If `cause` is given, must be multi-state (`Surv()` with a categorical event). Otherwise it must be right-censored (`Surv(time=..., event=...)`). An `Outcome` or a formula response such as `'Surv(time, status == 2)'` is also accepted, with its columns read from `data`. [risk]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Risk score or predicted cumulative incidence, one per subject. [cause]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer cause code for the competing-risks concordance. `None` (default) uses the standard right-censored concordance. [tau]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Truncation time. Defaults to the largest observed (cause-specific) event time. [conf_level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confidence level for the interval (default 0.95). [transform]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["logit"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Scale for the CI: `"logit"` (default, recommended), `"log"`, or `"identity"`. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A data frame (pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, a lazy frame, ...) holding the columns named by the response and `risk`. When `surv` is an `Outcome` or a formula, rows with a missing value in any column used are dropped first, along with the matching rows of any arrays passed alongside. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ConcordanceResult]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Point estimate, standard error, and confidence limits. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#46d914c2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") death = gw.Outcome.surv(time="time", event="status") cox = gw.CoxPH().fit(death, covariates=["age", "sex"], data=lung) lp = cox.predict(type="lp") gw.concordance_index_ci(death, risk=lp, data=lung) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ConcordanceResult(estimate=0.5959, se=0.0391, CI=[0.5176, 0.6696], conf_level=0.95) ``` ::: :::
